stories.title: Inside Ukrainian offensive pushing Russia back - with Starlink playing a key role
stories.body: The BBC joins Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi as it regains crucial territory in the Donbas, but optimism has been dampened by souring relations with President Trump.

stories.title: Palestinians and US journalist injured by Israeli settlers in West Bank harvest attack
stories.body: The BBC sees masked settlers attack Palestinians trying to harvest olives, amid a surge in similar incidents.

stories.title: Trump denies limiting Ukraine access to Starlink network
stories.body: Speed curbs limited Ukraine's defences against deadly Russian attacks on Tuesday night.

stories.title: Pope pictured for first time since surgery and cancer diagnosis
stories.body: The pontiff was diagnosed with lung cancer after having surgery at Rome's Gemelli Hospital on Tuesday.

stories.title: India's 'cockroach' party founder detained ahead of protest
stories.body: The youth-led movement had called for a Delhi protest after mass detentions last week and the jailing of two leaders.

stories.title: Dad fined after son, 2, died in Cyprus hotel fall
stories.body: Joshua Foster "lost control" of his son while showing him the view of a water park from a window.

stories.title: Ship attack reports near Hormuz reach record high as oil exports slow
stories.body: BBC Verify analysis of data from a UK maritime agency shows 12 vessels were struck in a week.

stories.title: Albanian protests turn violent: What we know
stories.body: Albania's capital Tirana has seen months of protests from an anti-government "Flamingo" movement, but what started on Tuesday this week was on a different scale.

stories.title: Patients in chains rescued from suspected illegal rehab centre in South Africa
stories.body: Some of the 200 patients were found with "sores all over their bodies" and in overcrowded rooms.

stories.title: China tells Israel to stop 'forced establishment' of West Bank settlements
stories.body: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi spoke to Israeli President Isaac Herzog on the sidelines of a conference.

stories.title: At least 33 pupils and teacher killed after school roof collapses in Pakistan
stories.body: Children were buried under the debris after the roof crashed through three classrooms, police say.

stories.title: Trump calls off livestream of Fort Hood attacker's execution by firing squad
stories.body: Trump said some would "rather not watch" the killing of Nidal Hasan, the first military execution in over 60 years.

stories.title: Tip-off foiled US teen suspect's plot to attack Hindu temple, police say
stories.body: The alleged plot only failed because the 19-year-old suspect's gun jammed outside the place of worship, say police.

stories.title: Bus hits train stopped on French side of Channel Tunnel, with 19 injured
stories.body: Two people were airlifted to hospital but no-one's life appeared to be in danger, officials said.

stories.title: Russia accuses Ukraine of attacking oil refinery after Zelensky says strikes to resume
stories.body: Ukraine's president says a pause on striking energy sites is over following fresh Russian attacks.

stories.title: Maduro pleads not guilty to new torture-related charges in New York
stories.body: "I reject this document entirely," Maduro said in court, responding to newly added torture-related charges.

stories.title: Houthi missile attack on Yemeni presidential palace kills five, minister says
stories.body: Yemen's information minister says the prime minister and other ministers were unhurt when ballistic missiles hit al-Maashiq Palace.

stories.title: Seven crew missing after drone attack leaves tanker ablaze off Romania's coast
stories.body: A search and rescue operation is under way in the Black Sea after the latest attack in the area.

stories.title: White House defends new press secretary over her legal credentials
stories.body: Katie Zacharia does not appear to be registered to the legal bar in any state where she has lived.

stories.title: School headscarf ban sparks rare protests in Azerbaijan and row with Turkey
stories.body: Protests have taken place over the rules which have seen pupils wearing hijabs turned away from schools.

🟡 **Mood: Cautious**  
Today's signals suggest a restrained optimism amid complex geopolitical and domestic tensions, with structural patterns favoring survival-focused and care-oriented dynamics. However, contested signals and low portfolio mood scores indicate underlying fragility and unresolved risks.

**1. Ukrainian Offensive and Starlink's Role**  
The Ukrainian counteroffensive against Russia, supported by Starlink's satellite network, emerges as the most structurally significant signal. This reflects a survival-focused trajectory, with Ukraine leveraging technological infrastructure to regain territorial control. The signal is grounded in verified outcomes, as reports confirm Russian positions being pushed back. While the direction is positive, the contestedness score highlights ongoing uncertainties, including Russia's potential countermeasures and the broader geopolitical implications of private-sector involvement in warfare. Structurally, this reinforces the trend of technology shaping modern conflict, with implications for global security paradigms.

**2. Hormuz Shipping Attacks and Oil Export Slowdowns**  
Reports of record-high ship attacks near the Strait of Hormuz signal escalating instability in a critical chokepoint for global energy flows. While the signal's priority score is low, its contestedness and contest score suggest significant disagreement about its trajectory. The fact-based nature of the headline confirms the attacks, but the broader implications—whether this reflects a short-term disruption or a longer-term trend—remain speculative. Structurally, this aligns with ongoing vulnerabilities in energy supply chains and underscores the need for resilience in global trade infrastructure.

**3. Domestic Signals: Foiled Attack and White House Defense**  
The thwarted plot to attack a Hindu temple in the US highlights the importance of proactive intelligence and community vigilance. While the signal is positive, its relatively low priority score suggests limited structural impact beyond immediate security concerns. Similarly, the White House's defense of its new press secretary underscores governance-oriented dynamics, with contested signals reflecting public scrutiny of leadership credentials. Both signals point to underlying tensions in domestic stability and governance, though their long-term trajectories remain unclear.

**4. Contested Signals and Broader Implications**  
Several signals, including the Hormuz attacks and the White House defense, exhibit contestedness, indicating unresolved debates about their direction and significance. These disagreements highlight the fragility of current trajectories, where positive developments coexist with underlying risks. The ensemble's cautious mood reflects this duality, emphasizing the need for vigilance in interpreting short-term gains within broader structural uncertainties.

**What to Watch Next**  
Monitor developments in Ukraine's offensive, particularly Russia's response and Starlink's continued role in military operations. In the Strait of Hormuz, track whether shipping disruptions escalate or stabilize, as this will clarify the trajectory of energy security risks. Domestically, pay attention to governance signals, including public reactions to leadership decisions and their implications for institutional stability.
